stories.title: Drupal Warns of New Highly Critical Site Takeover Vulnerability Under Active Exploitation
stories.abstract: CISA has added multiple vulnerabilities affecting Drupal core and GeoServer to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. These flaws, which include access bypass and injection issues, are currently being actively exploited in the wild, necessitating immediate attention from system administrators.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are confirmed to be under active exploitation, posing a high risk of unauthorized access or system compromise.
stories.action: Update Drupal to 10.6.23, 11.3.23, or 11.4.14; update GeoServer to 2.27.7, 2.28.6, or 3.0.2.

stories.title: Mitel security advisory (AV26-1212)
stories.abstract: Multiple vendors including Mitel, PostgreSQL, and SolarWinds have released security advisories addressing various vulnerabilities. These flaws impact OpenScape products, psqlODBC drivers, and SolarWinds Dameware and Serv-U software, ranging from memory corruption and command injection to privilege escalation.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities expose critical infrastructure and database drivers to remote exploitation, privilege escalation, and system instability.
stories.action: Update OpenScape, psqlODBC, Dameware, and Serv-U to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Unpatched Cacti Zero-Day Enables RCE in Just Four HTTP Requests via Guest Access
stories.abstract: A critical zero-day vulnerability in the Cacti network monitoring platform allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution. Proof-of-concept exploit code is currently circulating publicly, enabling potential system compromise without requiring valid credentials.
stories.why: Publicly available exploits for network monitoring tools significantly increase the risk of unauthorized infrastructure access and lateral movement within enterprise environments.
stories.action: Restrict network access to Cacti instances and monitor for suspicious command execution until an official patch is released.

stories.title: Juniper Networks security advisory (AV26-1101) – Update 1
stories.abstract: Juniper Networks has patched a critical command injection vulnerability in Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router software. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code with root-level privileges. CISA has confirmed the vulnerability is currently being exploited in the wild.
stories.why: This vulnerability grants full system control to attackers, posing a severe risk to network infrastructure and data integrity.
stories.action: Update Session Smart Conductor and Router to versions 7.0.5, 7.1.7, 7.2.3, or later immediately.

stories.title: Hackers reportedly infiltrated the Air Force's cloud systems
stories.abstract: Unauthorized actors compromised the U.S. Air Force's Cloud One platform. The intrusion was identified recently while personnel performed routine system upgrades. This incident follows a series of similar cyberattacks targeting various high-profile U.S. government agencies and federal departments.
stories.why: It highlights persistent vulnerabilities in critical government cloud infrastructure and the ongoing targeting of federal systems by sophisticated threat actors.

stories.title: Hackers Exploit 10 Vulnerabilities Across Mitel, Juniper, Vates, and Danfoss Products
stories.abstract: CISA has expanded its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog to include ten new security flaws. Among the additions are five vulnerabilities affecting Mitel MiCollab, including an arbitrary file upload issue, alongside bugs impacting products from Juniper, Vates, and Danfoss.
stories.why: Active exploitation of these vulnerabilities in enterprise infrastructure increases the risk of unauthorized access and potential system compromise.
stories.action: Review CISA KEV catalog and patch affected Mitel, Juniper, Vates, and Danfoss systems immediately.

stories.title: 1Password Hacked, Customer Data and Source Code Stolen in GitHub Account Breach
stories.abstract: 1Password reported a security breach involving its backend infrastructure. An unauthorized party compromised an employee's GitHub account to access limited customer support data. The company confirmed that user vaults, master passwords, and encrypted secrets remained secure and were not exposed during the incident.
stories.why: Supply chain and third-party account security remain critical vectors for attackers targeting service providers to gain unauthorized access to internal systems.

stories.title: Drupal Fail2Install Exploit Details Emerge as Critical RCE Flaw Faces Active Exploitation
stories.abstract: CISA has added a critical remote code execution vulnerability in Drupal core, known as Fail2Install, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw carries a CVSS score of 9.8 and is currently being actively exploited in the wild.
stories.why: This critical RCE allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code, posing a severe risk of full system compromise for Drupal-based infrastructure.
stories.action: Update Drupal core to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Recent Outages Have Economic Causes
stories.abstract: Recent widespread outages across major tech firms, airlines, and government agencies were not caused by coordinated cyberattacks or AI failures. Instead, these incidents highlight the inherent fragility of aging, centralized, and underfunded digital infrastructure that remains prone to coincidental, independent technical failures.
stories.why: It underscores systemic risks in critical infrastructure, emphasizing that complexity and technical debt often pose greater threats than malicious actors.

stories.title: SAP confirms security incident after suspicious GitHub activity
stories.abstract: SAP identified unauthorized access to its IT infrastructure involving compromised employee credentials. Attackers leveraged stolen GitHub tokens to gain access to internal repositories, potentially allowing them to view and modify proprietary source code.
stories.why: Compromised source code repositories can lead to the injection of backdoors or the discovery of vulnerabilities in widely used enterprise software.

stories.title: Remus malware steals Gmail messages via fake Google Sheets extension
stories.abstract: A new infostealer dubbed Remus is harvesting Gmail data by masquerading as a legitimate Google Sheets browser extension. Threat actors are promoting this capability as a zero-day exploit to compromise user email accounts through malicious Chrome add-ons.
stories.why: This highlights the persistent risk of browser-based supply chain attacks and the potential for malicious extensions to bypass standard email security controls.
stories.action: Audit installed Chrome extensions and remove any unauthorized or suspicious browser add-ons.

stories.title: pCloud confirms password manager hack after suspicious login alerts
stories.abstract: The pCloud Pass service experienced a security breach where unauthorized actors gained access to user accounts. Despite active two-factor authentication, victims reported suspicious device logins, suggesting a potential bypass or session hijacking technique was utilized by the attackers.
stories.why: Credential managers are high-value targets; a breach here compromises the entire security posture of affected users across all their stored accounts.
stories.action: Rotate all passwords stored in pCloud Pass and enable hardware-based security keys if supported.

stories.title: FIFA Says It Has Been Victim of a Cyberattack Accessing ‘Personal and Business Information’
stories.abstract: FIFA recently disclosed a security breach involving unauthorized access to a restricted subset of personal and business data. The organization has not provided specific details regarding the timing of the incident or the exact categories of information compromised.
stories.why: Large-scale organizations are frequent targets for data exfiltration, and the lack of transparency complicates risk assessment for partners and users.

stories.title: New NFS2ROOT Linux flaw can let attackers gain root privileges
stories.abstract: A long-standing vulnerability in the Linux kernel's Network File System server, identified as CVE-2026-99362, permits remote attackers to escalate privileges to root. The flaw has persisted in the codebase for over a decade, posing a significant risk to affected systems.
stories.why: Remote root access via NFS represents a critical compromise vector for enterprise infrastructure relying on network-attached storage.
stories.action: Apply the latest Linux kernel security patches immediately.

stories.title: New Boston Scientific data breach exposes personal, medical info
stories.abstract: Boston Scientific has begun notifying individuals that their personal and medical information was compromised during a recent cyberattack. The company is currently working to assess the full scope of the data exposure resulting from this security incident.
stories.why: Healthcare data breaches frequently lead to targeted phishing campaigns and identity theft, posing significant risks to affected patients and organizational reputation.

stories.title: Drupal warns of new site takeover flaw exploited in attacks
stories.abstract: Drupal developers issued a warning regarding a critical vulnerability that allows unauthorized site takeovers. This flaw stems from an incomplete fix in a previous installer patch, and active exploitation of the remaining security gap has already been observed in the wild.
stories.why: Unpatched Drupal instances are currently being targeted by attackers to gain full control over compromised websites.
stories.action: Update Drupal installations to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: In Other News: Tanker Cyberattacks, EU Quantum Act, New VirusTotal Capabilities
stories.abstract: Recent security incidents include a breach of USDA payment infrastructure, allegations that the RansomwareHelp service is profiting from ransom negotiations, and a successful cyberattack against the cybersecurity firm Radware.
stories.why: These incidents highlight ongoing risks to government financial systems and the potential for security vendors to become targets themselves.

stories.title: Japan’s education ministry discloses breach of government procurement system
stories.abstract: Japan's Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology reported a security breach affecting its procurement platform. Unauthorized actors accessed the system, potentially compromising sensitive business records and contact information belonging to government contractors and vendors.
stories.why: This incident highlights supply chain risks and the vulnerability of government procurement portals to unauthorized data exfiltration.

stories.title: Hackers Exploit N-able MailAssure Flaw While AI Agents Exploit MONAI Label Zero-Day
stories.abstract: CISA has added two critical vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following reports of active exploitation. The flaws include an SSRF vulnerability in N-able MailAssure and a zero-day impacting MONAI Label, both of which are currently being leveraged by malicious actors.
stories.why: Active exploitation of these vulnerabilities poses a significant risk to internal network infrastructure and sensitive data environments.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches provided by N-able and MONAI Label immediately.

stories.title: Hex Package Manager Warns of Potential Data Breach
Switzerland Confirms AI-Assisted Cyberattacks Breached Critical Infrastructure Operators
stories.abstract: Swiss cybersecurity officials confirmed that AI-driven agents successfully compromised two critical infrastructure operators. While these incidents represent the first documented use of AI-assisted attacks in the country, the breaches resulted in no significant operational disruptions.
stories.why: This marks a tangible shift toward the weaponization of AI agents in targeted attacks against essential industrial control systems.

stories.title: Microsoft Store App Found Delivering Vinci RAT Capable of Remote System Control
stories.abstract: Attackers are distributing a remote access trojan named Vinci RAT by masquerading as a legitimate sniping tool. The malicious installer, signed with a Microsoft certificate, is hosted on a deceptive website that redirects users to download the compromised application.
stories.why: The use of a valid Microsoft signature on malicious software bypasses standard security warnings, increasing the likelihood of successful endpoint compromise.
stories.action: Audit endpoint logs for unauthorized software installations originating from non-standard sniping tool domains.

stories.title: 100,000 Potentially Impacted by Colorado Data Breach
stories.abstract: Unauthorized actors gained access to the myColorado mobile application, compromising sensitive personal information uploaded by approximately 100,000 users. The state is currently investigating the extent of the data exposure within the digital identification and document storage platform.
stories.why: State-managed identity platforms are high-value targets for identity theft and credential harvesting, posing significant risks to the affected user base.

stories.title: British government takes services offline following ‘cyber incident’
stories.abstract: The UK Department for Work and Pensions proactively suspended several online services following a detected cyber incident. Officials confirmed that core pension and benefit disbursements remain operational and unaffected by the disruption.
stories.why: Government service outages often indicate potential unauthorized access or ransomware, necessitating monitoring for data exfiltration or service degradation.

stories.title: Malwarebytes Antivirus: Get 50% off during Black Friday 2026
Two Newly Disclosed GeoServer Vulnerabilities Under Attack
stories.abstract: Threat actors are actively exploiting two high-severity vulnerabilities within GeoServer. These flaws allow for unauthenticated remote code execution when chained with additional security weaknesses, putting exposed instances at significant risk of compromise.
stories.why: Unauthenticated remote code execution represents a critical risk, allowing attackers to gain full control over affected geospatial data servers.
stories.action: Update GeoServer to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ScreenConnect Flaw to Hijack MSP Technician PCs Without Warning
stories.abstract: Attackers are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in ConnectWise ScreenConnect, identified as CVE-2026-84869. This flaw allows unauthorized guests to execute malicious payloads on the host machines of MSP technicians, potentially granting full control over the targeted systems.
stories.why: MSP infrastructure is a high-value target for supply chain attacks, providing attackers with broad access to downstream client environments.
stories.action: Update ConnectWise ScreenConnect to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Suspected Vietnam-Linked Hackers Target Southeast Asia in South China Sea Espionage Campaign
stories.abstract: A state-sponsored threat actor identified as WeaveLotus is conducting espionage against government and military entities across Southeast Asia. The campaign focuses on gathering intelligence regarding regional defense policies and South China Sea territorial agreements, with confirmed activity targeting organizations in Thailand.
stories.why: This highlights ongoing geopolitical cyber-espionage risks for organizations operating in Southeast Asia or involved in regional defense and maritime policy.

stories.title: Cyberattack disrupts global news distribution platform at France’s AFP
North Korea-Linked PolinRider Poisons Over 7,600 GitHub Repositories to Spread Malware
stories.abstract: North Korean threat actors have compromised over 7,600 legitimate GitHub repositories to distribute malicious Python loaders. The campaign, active since February 2025, leverages authentic developer accounts to host and propagate secondary malware payloads across the software supply chain.
stories.why: This represents a significant supply chain risk where trusted, established repositories are weaponized to deliver malicious code to unsuspecting downstream users.
stories.action: Audit dependencies and verify the integrity of third-party code sourced from GitHub repositories.

stories.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ASP.NET Anti-CSRF Library Flaw Allowing Unauthenticated RCE
stories.abstract: A critical remote code execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-131914, has been identified in the legacy Idunno.AntiCsrf library for ASP.NET. Attackers are actively exploiting this flaw, which carries a CVSS score of 9.3, to compromise unauthenticated systems using versions 0.9.1.0 or 0.9.1 Beta.
stories.why: The vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote code execution, posing a severe risk of full system compromise for applications still utilizing this deprecated library.
stories.action: Remove the Idunno.AntiCsrf library from all applications immediately.

stories.title: Microsoft: Hackers in China, N Korea using ARTEX AI tool to break into global tech systems
stories.abstract: Microsoft reports that state-sponsored threat actors from China and North Korea are utilizing an offensive AI framework called ARTEX. This tool automates reconnaissance and exploitation tasks, significantly accelerating the speed at which attackers can compromise vulnerable systems.
stories.why: The integration of agentic AI into offensive toolkits lowers the barrier for complex attacks and drastically reduces the window for defensive response.

stories.title: VMware vCenter Hit by Another Critical 9.8-Rated Auth Bypass Flaw After Zero-Day Exploitation
stories.abstract: Broadcom released security updates for multiple VMware products to resolve 23 vulnerabilities. The most severe issue, CVE-2026-123903, is a critical authentication bypass flaw within the VMware Directory Service that carries a CVSS score of 9.8.
stories.why: Unauthenticated attackers can exploit this directory service flaw to compromise vCenter environments, posing a significant risk to virtualized infrastructure integrity.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches for VMware vCenter and related products immediately.

stories.title: Software giant SAP confirms cyber incident amid reports of source code breach
stories.abstract: SAP has acknowledged a security breach involving its software development environment. Unauthorized actors reportedly gained entry to the company's internal systems, raising concerns that proprietary source code may have been compromised during the intrusion.
stories.why: Compromised source code could facilitate the discovery of zero-day vulnerabilities or the creation of supply chain attacks targeting SAP's extensive enterprise customer base.

stories.title: Mitel MiCollab Zero-Days Exploited in Suspected AI-Assisted Attacks
stories.abstract: Threat actors leveraged previously undisclosed vulnerabilities in Mitel MiCollab software to facilitate extortion attempts. Researchers suggest the attackers utilized artificial intelligence to accelerate the exploitation process, successfully compromising targets before the vendor issued official security guidance or patches.
stories.why: The use of AI to weaponize zero-day vulnerabilities indicates a shift toward faster, more efficient exploitation cycles against enterprise communication infrastructure.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches from Mitel for MiCollab immediately.

stories.title: Critical Cisco Expressway Flaw Exploited in Attacks
stories.abstract: Cisco has confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-76466, a critical vulnerability affecting its Expressway Series and TelePresence Video Communication Server. The flaw carries a maximum CVSS score of 9.8 and allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code.
stories.why: This critical remote code execution vulnerability is currently being weaponized in the wild, posing an immediate risk to perimeter infrastructure.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches provided by Cisco immediately.

stories.title: Hackers Trojanize Official Q-Dir and DesktopOK Downloads to Deliver Remote Access Malware
stories.abstract: The official SoftwareOK website has been compromised, resulting in the distribution of trojanized installation files for Q-Dir and DesktopOK. Both fresh downloads and automated update mechanisms are currently delivering remote access malware to unsuspecting users.
stories.why: Supply chain compromises of legitimate utilities bypass traditional perimeter defenses and provide attackers with persistent, high-privilege access to end-user systems.
stories.action: Verify file hashes against known-good values and scan systems for unauthorized remote access tools.

stories.title: U.S. Treasury's Financial Crimes Agency Takes Some Systems Offline After Cyber Intrusion
Rackspace pulls plug on Spot cloud service after security breach
stories.abstract: Rackspace is shuttering its Spot cloud platform following a security incident. The company is forcing users to migrate their workloads and rotate credentials immediately, citing the breach as the primary reason for the sudden service termination.
stories.why: Sudden service shutdowns force emergency migrations, which often introduce misconfigurations, data exposure risks, and operational downtime for security teams.
stories.action: Migrate all workloads and rotate all credentials associated with the Rackspace Spot service immediately.
